title: Accounts Receivable Questions on the Payment Gap and Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements Late Fees
content:
**What is the payment gap of a Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements agreement?**
The payment gap is the number of calendar days from the date of the latest payment entry on the agreement to the fee date. The latest payment entry is the most recent payment on any of the agreement's invoices, whichever invoice it was applied to.

**How does the payment gap act on the late-fee rate?**
The payment gap raises the late-fee rate:

| Payment gap | Rise in the late-fee rate |
|---|---|
| 45 calendar days or more | 0.5 percentage points |
| 21 calendar days or more, and fewer than 45 | 0.25 percentage points |
| fewer than 21 calendar days | no rise |

The rise is added, in percentage points, to the late-fee rate itself, before the rate is applied to the unpaid amount past due.

**Is a gap of exactly 45 days a long gap?**
Yes. At 45 calendar days the rate rises by 0.5 percentage points; at 44 it rises by 0.25. Likewise a gap of exactly 21 days rises by 0.25 points, and one of 20 days does not rise.

**How are the days counted? (hypothetical dates)**
In calendar days from the date of the latest payment entry to the fee date. With a latest payment dated 1 March and a fee date of 15 April the gap is 45 days; with a fee date of 14 April it is 44 days; with a fee date of 22 March it is 21 days.

**Does a payment made to a different invoice from the one being charged count?**
Yes. The gap runs from the latest payment entry on the agreement, not from the latest payment on the invoice that carries the fee.
